decision.reason: Google's exact-timestamped Googlebook launch moved screen-aware and voice-aware Gemini features into a purchasable laptop platform. claims.text: Google's 21 September launch opened preorders for five partner Googlebooks and set October retail dates; the three launch posts were published at 13:00:00 UTC.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 RSS publication times; s3 availability; s4 five-model scope.

claims.text: Magic Pointer can be invoked over on-screen context, Rambler restructures spoken notes, and Googlebook also includes prompt-created widgets, proactive screen suggestions and background Gemini work.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 feature sections and s3 helpful-intelligence section.

claims.text: Google says Magic Pointer acts only when asked, stays off otherwise and can be switched off.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 Magic Pointer paragraph and s3 Magic Pointer bullet.

claims.text: 9to5Google reports that Gemini Nano produces AI descriptions of screenshots and that Magic Pointer, Rambler and Create My Widget operate through a hybrid intelligence architecture.
claims.sourceLocator: s7 For all Android always section and surrounding hands-on paragraphs.

claims.text: The public launch sources reviewed do not map, feature by feature, which screen or voice data remains local, which reaches cloud services, how long it is retained, whether it is used for model improvement, or which organisation-wide controls and logs exist.
claims.sourceLocator: Full relevant feature, security and product-page sections; the article limits the absence statement to the inspected source set and does not claim controls cannot exist elsewhere.

claims.text: Google's hardware-root, malware-detection, hypervisor and encrypted-phone-setup claims concern important platform protections, but they do not by themselves specify the data path or policy for each contextual AI request.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises are s3 setup and security sections and s5's separate local/cloud processing distinction; the bounded control distinction is Index Us synthesis.

claims.text: An NPU rating and the presence of Gemini Nano do not establish that every AI feature runs entirely on the laptop.
claims.sourceLocator: s4 NPU claim, s5 local/cloud distinction, s6 Magic Pointer internet requirement and s7 hybrid-architecture reporting support the narrow inference.

claims.text: Google says Googlebooks reach Australian retail on 5 October 2026.
claims.sourceLocator: Pricing and availability sections in s2, s3 and s4.

claims.text: Teams handling confidential screens should require a per-feature data-flow and control matrix, then test the shipping device, before broad deployment.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises are the documented context access, invocation boundary, incomplete service-data map and hybrid design; the recommendation is not a finding that Googlebook is unsafe.

claims.text: Current independent reporting includes hands-on use but no reproducible privacy or security evaluation of the shipping platform.
claims.sourceLocator: Scope of the three independent launch reports and the retained public-source search; the statement is limited to evidence found and reviewed in this run.

claims.text: Google's current product page says Magic Pointer requires an internet connection, is available to users aged 18 and over, and can return variable results; this rules out treating Magic Pointer as fully offline but does not identify transmitted fields, processing split, retention or administration controls.
claims.sourceLocator: s6 Magic Pointer feature card and footnote 4; the narrow offline inference is bounded in the article.
